::: {.solutions}

The TMUA gives you **no formula booklet and no calculator**, so everything on this page has to come out of
your head on the day. That is why you are writing it rather than being handed it: [a sheet you filled in
yourself is remembered far better than one you were given]{.hl}.

## How to use this

**Do not sit down and fill it all in at once.** Build it up across the course:

1. **After every session and every past paper**, ask one question: *did I have to stop and reconstruct a
   formula?* If yes, it goes in the table — in your own words.
2. **Only write what you actually needed.** A formula you have never used will not stick.
3. **★ marks the ones that appear on almost every paper.** If nothing else is finished by October, finish
   those.
4. Each section has a **workspace** underneath — use it for the ones that need a diagram, an example, or
   more than one line.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Where to start.** Sections 1–2 (algebra, sequences) first — those are what 2020 Paper 1 uses.
Sections 4, 6, 7 follow the trig and calculus papers. Section 9 is Paper 2 only.

Stuck? The completed version is at **[Formula Sheet](formula_sheet.qmd)** — but write your own attempt
**first**, then check. Copying it straight across defeats the point.
:::

## 8 · Graphs and transformations &nbsp; *(MM8)*

Fill in the effect on $y = \mathrm f(x)$:

| Transformation | Effect on the graph |
|---|---|
| $\mathrm f(x) + a$ | |
| $\mathrm f(x + a)$ | |
| $a\,\mathrm f(x)$ | |
| $\mathrm f(ax)$ | |
| $-\mathrm f(x)$ | |
| $\mathrm f(-x)$ | |
| "For which $k$…" question ★ — the three steps | |

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**The two that catch people** are $\mathrm f(x+a)$ and $\mathrm f(ax)$ — write *why* they do the opposite
of what they look like.
:::
